mech_h3: We have never been on the other side.
mech_p: This firm has never represented an insurance company. Robert Hindin has practiced in California since 1975. Kyle Hindin, from the day he was licensed in 2016, has only represented injured people. When the adjuster calls, they're not talking to someone who once sat on their side. They're talking to the other team.
ins_h2: They're friendly. They're not on your side.
ins_p1: The adjuster's job is to close your {City} claim cheap. It's not a conspiracy. It's the business.
ins_l1: They'll ask for a recorded statement while you're still on pain medication.
ins_l2: They'll offer money before anyone knows whether you need an MRI.
ins_l3: If you wait to see a doctor, they'll say you “weren't that hurt.”
ins_l4: They'll say you were partly at fault to trim the check. California's comparative fault lets them try. You don't have to accept their percentage.
ins_p3: You don't need to become an expert in that playbook while your body is trying to heal. That's what you hire us for.
tactic_1_b: Everything you say gets used. Don't give one.
tactic_2_b: It's sized for someone without a lawyer.
tactic_3_b: Waiting “to see if it goes away” becomes their argument.
tactic_4_b: California lets you recover even if you were partly at fault. Don't sign their version.
time_h2: Waiting is the most expensive thing you can do.
time_p1: California generally gives you two years from the crash to sue. If the crash involves the city, the county, or a transit agency, you may have only six months to file a government claim. Miss it and the case can die no matter how badly you were hurt.
time_p2: The clock that actually kills cases is faster than the law:
time_l1: Store and freeway cameras overwrite in days
time_l3: The other driver “remembers” a different story after talking to their insurer
time_l4: You wait to see a doctor, and they call that a gap
time_p3: Call now. If there's no case, we'll tell you. If there is, we send the letters to preserve the video while it still exists.

rev_1_q: Kyle, Abby, and Ismael… All we had to do was sign the initial paperwork, and they did everything else. They got us to a doctor the very next day… dealt with the insurance so that we didn’t have to.
rev_2_q: They made me feel like family… I was injured and trying to recover, and they took care of both me and my wife. They fought for us.
rev_3_q: Kyle and Corbin were extremely helpful during a very vulnerable time… made sure the stress load was taken off of me as I was trying to recover.
faq_1_a: Nothing up front. No attorney fee unless we recover. Case costs are explained before you sign.
faq_2_q: They already offered me a check.
faq_2_a: Don't cash it. The first offer is sized for someone who doesn't have a lawyer yet. Free case review. If the check was fair, we'll tell you. It almost never is.
faq_3_a: You can still have a claim. In California, comparative fault reduces what you collect — it doesn't erase it. Don't accept the adjuster's percentage.
faq_4_q: Will I have to go to court?
faq_4_a: Most cases settle. We prepare as if they won't. That's why the number moves.
faq_5_q: I don't have papers / I didn't go to the ER / I don't speak English.
faq_5_a: Call anyway. California law doesn't take away your claim because of immigration status. If you didn't see a doctor the same day, there's still a case — waiting longer makes it worse. And you don't need English: Ismael is on the team.
step_1_b: One call or the form. A real person, not a menu.
step_2_b: We talk to the adjuster, request the video, help you get to a doctor. You rest.
step_3_b: We negotiate the maximum. If they won't pay, we litigate. No attorney fee unless we recover.
